THEOREM/INPUT: conditional on declared historyH, an ACTUAL m-row old archive is exchangeable; its labels are finite binary strings, potentially on a COUNTABLE alphabet. The target Q_H is fixed givenH; new target samples/fresh bits are conditionally independent of the archive. No finite explicit alphabet or IID old-row hypothesis is needed for the OUTPUT law. Target choice from a permutation-invariant history such as the archive histogram is allowed if conditional exchangeability actually holds. Arbitrary ordered-row/adaptive history is not automatically allowed. This is a stronger BATCH contract, not the one-distinguished-old-X theorem.

CONSTRUCTION: collect m independent target labels, compute the two finite observed histogramsA,B using only present labels. Within each old-label class retain a uniform min(Ai,Bi) subset of ORIGINAL row indices; assign the residual target multiset uniformly to unmatched rows. No alphabet enumeration occurs. Conditional onH,A,B, the old archive is uniform over its finite permutation type; the operation is row-permutation equivariant and produces target countsB. Therefore the entire output vector is uniform over typeB. Averaging the actual multinomial target counts gives EXACT law Q_H^m conditional onH. This proves joint independence conditional onH, not merely individual marginals; unconditional mixing overrandomH need not be IID. Changed fraction is EXACTLY TV(A/m,B/m). A true-population near-maximal guarantee still requires a bound on old empirical fluctuations/effective support; exchangeability alone gives no such rate. Strong correlation can make themlarge.

FAIR-BIT ISSUE: uniformsubset/permutation selection is exact using ordinary integerrejection but has unbounded random-bit length. Source-query capm does not itself give an every-run bit cap. There are at most2m integerdraws of range<=m; each proposal uses at mostceil(log2 m) bits and succeeds withprobability>=1/2. Cap each draw at r=ceil(log2(8m/epsilon)) proposals. If a cap fails, output the already-acquired target list in its original order. The capped and exact reference algorithms coincide except on probability<=2m*2^-r<=epsilon/4. Thus the capped output law is within epsilon/4 of Q_H^m; all output labels remain among actual target draws, even on fallback. No exactness of a runtime-selected fallback is falsely asserted.

DDB1/SCC COROLLARY: use accepted exact-supp
